subject: DataForge Dedicated: provisioning handshake and autoscale alignment
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@dataforge.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: initial GPU pool sizing + autoscale thresholds

Hi Samir —

Great talking yesterday. Per our call, attached is the draft SOW (DataForge_SOW_v1.pdf) and a first-pass recommendation for the Dedicated GPU pool you asked about. High-level recap:

- Workload: low-latency text generation + embedding lookups for customer-facing API (p95 latency target 150ms).
- Initial pool: 8 x A100-80GB equivalent (shared prefix caching across workers) — recommended to cover sustained baseline of ~350k tokens/min with headroom for steady growth.
- Autoscale: scale up in increments of 2 GPUs when sustained token rate > 70% of baseline for 3 minutes, burst policy allows +4 GPUs for 10 minute windows with cooldown.
- Multi-region: primary in us-west1, failover to us-central with automatic routing (we'll confirm network egress and cross-region latency impact).

Ask from your side: can you confirm expected peak tokens/minute (or requests/sec and average tokens/request) and whether you expect >10% of traffic to come from EU during launch. That will determine if we recommend a second regional pool or cross-region QoS.

I've looped in Irene (implementation lead) and Monica (CS ops) to pick up net requirements and activation timeline.

Attachments: [Attachment: DataForge_SOW_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@dataforge.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: DataForge Engineering <eng@dataforge.ai>, Elena Petrov <procurement@dataforge.ai>
Date: 2025-08-04T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: initial GPU pool sizing + autoscale thresholds

Thanks Ben — good summary. A few data points from our side:

- Baseline request profile: ~18 rps average, median 120 tokens/request, bursty peaks up to 120 rps during specific batch inference windows.
- Expected growth: +40% over first 3 months (product marketing launch).
- Regional split at launch: ~92% US, 6% EU, 2% APAC. We do plan to add an EU pool for Q4 but want a single-region launch first.

Questions/concerns:
1) How does the burst +4 GPUs affect committed vs metered billing? Will burst consumption be billed at a different rate? Elena from procurement is cc'd — she will want a clear table of committed units vs burstable units.
2) We have strict network security needs — our infra team will need a network diagram and the list of required firewall rules and peering details.

Irene/Redwood team — please advise on the net/ops checklist and any SOC2 or compliance artifacts you require.

- Samir
Samir Shah
Head of Infrastructure, DataForge
samir.shah@dataforge.ai
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@dataforge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-05T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: initial GPU pool sizing + autoscale thresholds

Hi Samir — thanks for the numbers, that's really helpful. A few clarifications and the implementation asks from our side: 

1) Pool sizing rationale — with your profile (18 rps median, peaks to 120 rps): the 8 GPU baseline covers sustained demand with our continuous batching. Given your 120 rps burst windows, the burst +4 GPUs should cover short spikes; however, for the planned +40% growth, we recommend an upgrade path to 12 GPUs in month 2 if growth becomes steady.

2) Billing model — committed baseline (8 GPUs) billed per your committed-capacity contract; burst GPUs are metered and billed at the metered rate (we will provide a line-item comparison in the SOW v2). Short bursts (<=10 minutes) are billed per-minute; if bursts are sustained beyond the cooldown windows they are billed as capacity usage. I'll ask Ben to include a committed vs burst table.

3) Network/security checklist — attaching a simple diagram and the initial firewall/peering checklist we need from DataForge. Please have your netops confirm:
   - Outbound peering CIDR ranges for the pool (we'll need to allow inbound from those ranges if you want private connectivity).
   - TLS mutual-auth options and KMS integration (we support customer-managed CMK via AWS KMS or GCP KMS; let us know which you'd prefer).
   - Audit/log shipping: we'll need the endpoint to push audit logs (S3/GCS) for retention if you opt-in.

Attachment: [Attachment: network_diagram.png (image/png)]

4) Compliance docs — we maintain a SOC 2 Type II package and can share a redacted report under an NDA / secure link. Marissa will coordinate the secure share.

Next steps proposal:
- Action: DataForge to confirm tokens/request and netops contact + preferred KMS provider (reply inline).
- Action: Redwood to produce SOW v2 including committed vs burst billing table and a detailed activation checklist (I aim to have this by EOD 2025-08-06).

I propose a short kickoff next Tuesday 8/12 10am PT to walk through the checklist. Does that work for your team?

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@dataforge.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-06T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: initial GPU pool sizing + autoscale thresholds

Thanks everyone — adding a few timeline details from CS ops and intake: 

- Staging pool (4 GPUs) can be provisioned in parallel to baseline pick-up; we recommend a 2-week smoke test window before flip.
- Implementation milestones (proposed):
   • Week 0 (kickoff): confirm netops contact + SOW signoff
   • Week 1: staging pool provision + network peering test
   • Week 2: smoke tests, latency verification, prefix/KV cache warm-up
   • Week 3: baseline pool flip and monitoring runbook handoff

Links: HubSpot deal + kickoff doc: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/DF-2025-0423
DocuSign SOW (v1): https://app.docusign.com/signon?e=example-sow-DF-0423

Irene: we'll need the activation runbook and a readiness checklist to share with your netops group at staging start. Ben: can you confirm internal E2E testing windows for the staging pool?

Monica
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
From: Elena Petrov <procurement@dataforge.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Samir Shah <samir.shah@dataforge.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-07T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: initial GPU pool sizing + autoscale thresholds

Thanks — quick procurement question before we escalate to legal: please confirm expected monthly cost ranges for (a) committed 8 GPUs, (b) committed 8 + typical burst consumption (we estimate bursts add ~15% extra), and (c) a scenario where bursts are sustained for >24 hours (how is that handled contractually). Also confirm the minimum term for reserved capacity and whether credits apply for outages exceeding SLA.

We prefer those numbers in a single spreadsheet row per scenario.

Elena
Procurement, DataForge
procurement@dataforge.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Petrov <procurement@dataforge.ai>, Samir Shah <samir.shah@dataforge.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-10T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: initial GPU pool sizing + autoscale thresholds

Elena — understood. Attached is the updated SOW v2 (DataForge_SOW_v2.pdf) with a committed vs burst pricing table and examples for sustained-burst scenarios. Short answers inline: 

- Committed 8 GPUs: see SOW v2 row A. Minimum term: 6 months with monthly billing; annual commitment discount available.
- Typical burst +15%: metered at the burst rate column (we bill per-minute for metered bursts). SOW includes an example invoice calculation for 15% sustained bursts in a 30-day period.
- Sustained >24 hours: if bursts convert to persistent usage beyond agreed cooldowns our billing converts that consumption to reserved equivalent and we propose a retroactive invoice adjustment (we capture usage and discuss with procurement before converting to new committed unit).
- SLA credits: included in enterprise terms; credits tiered by monthly availability thresholds (SOW v2 Appendix B).

I've asked finance to prepare the single-line spreadsheet summary and will drop it into the HubSpot deal row.

Action items (final):
- DataForge: confirm netops contact + preferred KMS provider (AWS KMS or GCP KMS) by EOD 8/12.
- Redwood: finalize SOW v2 and share DocuSign link (done).
- Schedule kickoff 8/12 10am PT — Irene to send invite.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
